why: Node loads the module named by its preload option (-r, --require, --import, --loader) before the entry, so the file behind it runs exactly as an entry does. The rule skipped that value as an option value, and a postinstall that preloads a tracked file whose code starts the Claude Code CLI with its permission prompts skipped passed with a note. Both sides track the same scripts/t.js. On the fail side the postinstall preloads it and names no entry; on the pass side only the lint script preloads it, which a person starts on purpose, and the file is a warning. Whoever skips the preload value turns the fail side green; whoever fails every code file with the switch turns the pass side red. Content is base64 because rebar reads its own caso.json raw.
